automotive-ev-battery.title: Top Selling Electric Vehicles in the World — 27% EV Share in July!
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Global plug-in vehicle registrations increased 7% year-over-year in July, reaching approximately 1.8 million units with battery electric vehicles (BEVs) growing 16% while plug-in hybrids declined 11%. Electric vehicles achieved a 27% market share, demonstrating accelerating EV adoption and shifting market dynamics between pure electric and hybrid technologies.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Hyundai Bets Big On Extended-Range Electric Vehicles
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Hyundai is significantly expanding its focus on extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs), a category that has become increasingly important in China due to recent policy changes. The company is developing vehicles that combine small electric motors and battery systems with conventional combustion engines to serve growing market demand.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Asahi Kasei's pre-doping technology cuts first-cycle capacity loss in silicon-rich cells
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Asahi Kasei has developed a lithium pre-doping technology for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries with silicon-based anodes that reduces permanent capacity loss during the first charge cycle. This advancement addresses a critical barrier to higher energy density batteries needed for EV applications.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Bentley Launches Its Very First — No, Second — No, Third — Electric Car
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Bentley has introduced the Torcal SUV, its first fully electric vehicle produced entirely in-house, targeting urban drivers with luxury specifications and high-end features. This launch marks a significant milestone in the automaker's electrification strategy and expansion into the premium EV market.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Emobi and OmniTrust partner to advance Plug & Charge adoption
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Emobi and OmniTrust have partnered to advance Plug & Charge adoption, a charging standard gaining traction in North America built on the ISO 15118 protocol. Emobi's cloud-based JustPlug system represents an important step toward standardized, seamless EV charging experiences across roaming networks.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Generational finds cell-voltage imbalance in one in 85 used EVs tested in the UK
automotive-ev-battery.summary: UK-based EV battery diagnostics company Generational analyzed cell-level data from approximately 10,000 used-EV battery tests, finding that roughly one in 85 vehicles displayed significant cell-voltage imbalances above 50 mV. This research highlights critical considerations for battery health assessment in the growing used EV market.

automotive-ev-battery.title: XPENG Drives Physical AI To Next Level
automotive-ev-battery.summary: XPeng has announced major developments in its physical AI initiatives, including advancements in its IRON humanoid robot and VLA 2.0 intelligent driving technology. These technological breakthroughs position the company for expanded growth, though many developments remain in pre-revenue stages.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Lucid's 'fire risk' recall was for LED lights & already fixed by a July software update
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Lucid's recall of 27,000 vehicles for an apparent fire risk involved an electronic fuse controlling LED lights that could overheat, though the issue was already resolved through a software update distributed in July. The incident underscores the importance of transparent communication regarding EV safety recalls.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Slate will offer a high roof cargo version of its compact pickup – and you can buy it!
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Bezos-backed Slate Auto announced detailed plans for a high roof cargo version of its electric compact pickup truck, signaling serious commercial vehicle market ambitions. The company's Fleet Business Development team showcased the vehicle at a Portland ride-along event.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Revolutionizing commercial EVs: megawatt charging and its implications
automotive-ev-battery.summary: This analysis explores the growing demand for megawatt charging solutions in the commercial EV industry, examining technical requirements, cost implications, and performance advantages. Megawatt charging is increasingly recognized as critical infrastructure for accelerating commercial vehicle electrification.

tech-ai.title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
tech-ai.summary: Caterpillar is leveraging decades of experience with autonomous systems in remote mining operations to inform its approach to broader AI deployment. The industrial equipment manufacturer's proven track record in autonomous machine automation positions it as a significant player in enterprise AI implementation.

tech-ai.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
tech-ai.summary: Major music publishers Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed a lawsuit against AI company Anthropic, alleging copyright infringement of tens of thousands of works with potential damages reaching several billion dollars. The suit seeks up to $150,000 per work and $25,000 for each instance of stripped copyright data, marking the latest in a series of legal challenges against AI firms over training data.

tech-ai.title: Inside Meta's push to put robots to work in data centers
tech-ai.summary: Meta is testing robots to automate tasks traditionally performed by data center technicians, expanding the company's deployment of robotics in its infrastructure operations. This initiative reflects the tech industry's broader push toward automation in large-scale computational facilities.

tech-ai.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
tech-ai.summary: Texas Governor Greg Abbott has frozen state spending on Flock's AI surveillance cameras following mounting backlash from across the political spectrum over privacy concerns. The move comes as investigations reveal the state spent over $30 million on the camera network, funded through a $1 insurance policy surcharge ostensibly for catalytic converter theft prevention.

tech-ai.title: TechCrunch Mobility: The hidden human cost of robotaxis
tech-ai.summary: TechCrunch examines the societal and workforce implications of autonomous taxi technology as AI-driven robotaxis continue to enter the transportation market. The investigation explores often-overlooked human costs associated with this technological transition.

tech-ai.title: China's robots race ahead
tech-ai.summary: China has demonstrated significant advancement in humanoid robotics development, with robots competing in the World Humanoid Robot Games, underscoring the intensifying U.S.-China competition in artificial intelligence and robotics. The achievement highlights China's growing technological capabilities in autonomous systems.

tech-ai.title: Enormous 12TB Steam leak includes abandoned Half-Life 2: Episode 3 assets
tech-ai.summary: A massive 12-terabyte data breach has exposed over a decade of Steam game builds and development assets from 2003 to 2013, including unreleased content from Half-Life 2: Episode 3, Portal 2 cut content, and experimental titles from both Valve and third-party developers. The leak provides a significant window into game development history and cancelled projects.

tech-ai.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to study dark matter and dark energy
tech-ai.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has successfully launched and begun its three-month journey to the L2 orbital point, where it will conduct an unprecedented survey of the universe with a field of view 100 times larger than the Hubble Space Telescope. The mission represents a major advancement in cosmological research following past funding challenges.

tech-ai.title: Musk's faster path to more gas turbines comes with pollution problem
tech-ai.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX plans to establish a secretive foundry to manufacture turbine blades in-house, accelerating gas turbine deployment by 18 months compared to traditional timelines. However, the expansion of gas power infrastructure has generated legal challenges and health concerns regarding pollution in communities where such turbines are deployed.

tech-ai.title: Two new small, powerful Macs
tech-ai.summary: Apple has released new compact Mac models offering increased performance capabilities, continuing the company's strategy of offering diverse form factors and price points in its computer lineup. The updates reflect ongoing refinement of Apple's silicon-based architecture.

science-space.title: NASA's Dark Universe-Seeking Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
science-space.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope successfully launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center, beginning a three-month journey to its final orbit one million miles away. The mission will reveal insights into the universe's darkest secrets through its large field of view and advanced imaging capabilities.

science-space.title: Liftoff! NASA's Roman Space Telescope soars to the stars on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket in spectacular launch
science-space.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope successfully launched into space atop a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on August 30, marking the beginning of a new era for astronomy and our understanding of the cosmos. The telescope is poised to revolutionize research into dark energy and the universe's fundamental structure.

science-space.title: Lift-off! NASA launches Roman Space Telescope to tackle dark-energy mysteries
science-space.summary: NASA has successfully launched the Roman Space Telescope, a mission dedicated to investigating the mysteries of dark energy and expanding humanity's understanding of the universe. The telescope represents a major advancement in observational astronomy and cosmological research.

science-space.title: 'What a glorious dawn launch': Why the Roman Space Telescope's picture-perfect liftoff beyond Earth is such a big deal
science-space.summary: The Roman Space Telescope achieved a picture-perfect launch, marking a significant milestone in astronomical research and exploration. The successful deployment sets the stage for groundbreaking discoveries about the universe's composition and evolution.

science-space.title: NASA Deep Space Network's New Goldstone Antenna Goes Online
science-space.summary: NASA's Deep Space Network has completed and activated Deep Space Station 23, a 34-meter multifrequency beam-waveguide antenna at the Goldstone complex in California. This new antenna will significantly enhance NASA's deep space communications capabilities and expand the DSN's capacity for decades to come.

science-space.title: Hundreds of hidden earthquakes found at Antarctica's Doomsday Glacier
science-space.summary: Researchers have detected 245 previously overlooked seismic events beneath Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier, many triggered by massive icebergs breaking off and colliding with the glacier. The surge in glacial earthquakes coincided with periods of accelerated ice flow toward the ocean, suggesting that changing ocean conditions may be destabilizing this critical ice sheet.

science-space.title: A solution to the mystery of the missing neutrinos
science-space.summary: Researchers have made progress in solving the long-standing mystery of missing neutrinos in astrophysics, potentially reshaping our understanding of particle physics and stellar processes. The findings address a significant gap in the Standard Model of particle physics.

science-space.title: Ribbon-Cutting Event for NASA Deep Space Network's Deep Space Station 23
science-space.summary: NASA leadership and personnel celebrated the completion of Deep Space Station 23 at the Goldstone complex with a formal ribbon-cutting ceremony on August 25, 2026. The new 34-meter antenna represents a major infrastructure upgrade for the Deep Space Network.

science-space.title: Animal-microbe partnerships date back to the dawn of complex life
science-space.summary: New research reveals that symbiotic relationships between animals and microorganisms originated during the earliest stages of complex life on Earth. The discovery provides important insights into the evolution of life and the fundamental nature of biological cooperation.

science-space.title: On this day in space! Aug. 30, 1992: Astronomers discover 1st Kuiper Belt object out beyond Pluto
science-space.summary: Thirty-four years ago on August 30, 1992, astronomers made the historic discovery of 1992 QB-1, the first confirmed object orbiting the sun beyond Pluto, fundamentally changing our understanding of the solar system's structure. This discovery marked the beginning of the modern era of Kuiper Belt exploration and revealed the existence of a vast region of icy bodies.

finance-markets.title: Rising bond yields add tens of billions to G7 countries' debt costs
finance-markets.summary: The world's largest developed economies are facing significantly elevated financing costs for their debt following escalating US-Iran tensions and rising bond yields. This fiscal pressure threatens to weigh heavily on public finances across the G7 bloc during a period of already strained government budgets.

finance-markets.title: Asian Stocks Drop on Hawkish Warsh Tone, Oil Gains: Markets Wrap
finance-markets.summary: Asian equity markets declined following hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, which strengthened market expectations for an interest-rate increase in the coming month. The dollar maintained its gains while oil prices climbed amid intensifying Middle East tensions.

finance-markets.title: US and Iran exchange fire for the first time in more than a month
finance-markets.summary: The United States and Iran engaged in direct military action for the first time in over a month, with American forces striking an island in the Strait of Hormuz followed by Iranian retaliation. The escalation triggered notable increases in oil prices amid concerns over regional stability and global energy supplies.

finance-markets.title: Big Tech profits get $160bn boost from gains on stakes in other AI companies
finance-markets.summary: Large technology companies have received approximately $160 billion in paper gains from their investments in artificial intelligence firms including OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX. Analysts caution that these substantial windfalls have obscured underlying earnings metrics in the tech sector, complicating accurate performance assessment.

finance-markets.title: Gold Steadies After Tumbling as Warsh Spurs Fed Rate-Hike Bets
finance-markets.summary: Gold prices stabilized following a decline exceeding 3% as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's commitment to combating inflation bolstered expectations for near-term interest rate increases by the central bank. The precious metal's weakness reflects investor reassessment of monetary policy trajectories in response to Fed communications.

finance-markets.title: Oil rises over 1% after U.S. forces strike two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island
finance-markets.summary: Oil prices rose more than 1% as escalating tensions in the Middle East intensified supply disruption concerns following U.S. military strikes against Iranian positions on Larak Island. The geopolitical conflict continues to inject volatility and risk premiums into global energy markets.

finance-markets.title: Shein Set for Long-Awaited Hong Kong IPO Debut
finance-markets.summary: Ultra-fast fashion retailer Shein is proceeding with a highly anticipated Hong Kong initial public offering at a valuation significantly reduced from its previous $100 billion peak. The company is undertaking a radical business model overhaul in response to regulatory crackdowns on tax loopholes and margin compression in the digital retail sector.

finance-markets.title: Indian Billionaire Taps $700 Million Private Credit for Megha Buyout
finance-markets.summary: A major shareholder of India's Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd. is raising approximately $700 million from global private credit investors to acquire his uncle's stake in the company in what would constitute one of India's largest transactions this year. The deal reflects growing utilization of private credit markets for large-scale corporate transactions in the Indian market.

finance-markets.title: Taiwan's Top Regulator Wants to Wean Taiwan's Insurers Off US Dollar Dependence
finance-markets.summary: Taiwan's financial regulator is targeting the overhaul of a decades-long investment model employed by the island's life insurance firms, which collectively represent one of the world's largest insurance capital pools with heavy dollar exposure. The regulatory shift aims to reduce currency dependence and manage systemic risks in Taiwan's insurance sector.

finance-markets.title: MSCI Rebalancing Threatens to Turn 'Messy' in New Indian Auction
finance-markets.summary: India's recently implemented closing auction system faces its most significant test yet as billions of dollars in passive fund trades are routed through the new mechanism. Market participants express concerns that the system may struggle with the massive volume of index rebalancing trades, potentially creating operational challenges and market disruptions.

world-news.title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island in first known attack in weeks
world-news.summary: The United States conducted military strikes against Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) rocket launchers on Larak Island, marking the first known US attack on Iran since late July. Iran reported that the strikes resulted in civilian casualties, escalating tensions in an already volatile region.

world-news.title: Iran war live: IRGC attacks US bases in Jordan after US bombs Larak Island
world-news.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched attacks against US military bases in Jordan in response to American strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island. The escalating military exchange represents a significant intensification of US-Iran hostilities.

world-news.title: What are the implications of the US-Venezuela oil deal?
world-news.summary: The United States and Venezuela have reached an oil agreement amid opposition within Venezuela, with interim leadership asserting the deal will support the country's economic recovery. The agreement represents a significant shift in US-Venezuela relations and has major implications for hemispheric energy markets.

world-news.title: 'Opening a new chapter': Syria reopens embassy in Libya after talks
world-news.summary: Syria and Libya have agreed to reopen their diplomatic missions following bilateral talks between the Syrian foreign minister and Libyan prime minister. The agreement includes establishing a cooperation committee and represents a significant development in restoring diplomatic relations between the two nations.

world-news.title: Russia says it helped to repel Niger attempted coup
world-news.summary: Russia claims it assisted Niger's authorities in thwarting an attempted military coup early Saturday morning at a key military base. The incident underscores ongoing geopolitical competition in West Africa and Russia's expanding security role on the continent.

world-news.title: Iceland votes against restarting EU membership talks
world-news.summary: Icelandic voters rejected a government proposal to resume European Union accession negotiations, with 52.8 percent voting against the measure in a referendum. The decision reflects public sentiment toward EU membership and shapes Iceland's long-term European integration strategy.

world-news.title: Vote count starts in Guinea-Bissau referendum on strengthening presidency
world-news.summary: Guinea-Bissau has begun tallying votes in a referendum on expanding presidential powers, held ten months after a military coup. The military leadership contends the referendum is designed to stabilize future civilian governance following the constitutional crisis.

world-news.title: Zambian opposition leader charged with treason
world-news.summary: A Zambian opposition leader has been charged with treason after previously seeking refuge at a United Nations building in the capital. The prosecution reflects ongoing political tensions and rule-of-law concerns in the southern African nation.

world-news.title: Israeli strike kills 3-year-old child in Gaza
world-news.summary: An Israeli military strike on Deir el-Balah in Gaza killed at least two Palestinians, including a three-year-old child. The incident continues the cycle of civilian casualties in the ongoing Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

world-news.title: Eight killed and others missing after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
world-news.summary: A search and rescue operation is underway after a ferry carrying approximately 270 people capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus, with at least eight confirmed deaths and several others reported missing. The maritime incident has prompted an international emergency response.

crypto-web3.title: Crypto.com-linked Cronos network halts after Tectonic exploit estimated at $75 million
crypto-web3.summary: The Cronos network halted operations following a significant security exploit affecting the Tectonic lending protocol, with losses estimated at $75 million. The attacker manipulated the illiquid TONIC token's price to artificially inflate collateral before executing a borrow attack, echoing previous exploits in decentralized finance protocols.

crypto-web3.title: Polygon Quietly Patched Security Flaws in Two Hard Forks Before Disclosing Them
crypto-web3.summary: Polygon deployed security patches through its Austin and Kyoto hard forks to address denial-of-service and consensus vulnerabilities before public disclosure. The network stated that the flaws were never exploited, but the delayed transparency raised questions about responsible disclosure practices in blockchain development.

crypto-web3.title: Chainalysis accuses ICE of unfairly steering $95 million blockchain contract to TRM Labs
crypto-web3.summary: Chainalysis filed a lawsuit challenging the Intercontinental Exchange's $95 million blockchain analytics contract award to competitor TRM Labs, alleging unfair procurement practices. The legal action requests a federal court block the contract and compel ICE to conduct open competition.

crypto-web3.title: Michael Saylor hints at first bitcoin purchase in two months
crypto-web3.summary: MicroStrategy CEO Michael Saylor signaled a potential resumption of Bitcoin acquisitions following a two-month pause, as the cryptocurrency rallied above $79,000 and Bitcoin dominance climbed above 60%. Saylor's "We're Back" post fueled market speculation about the company's next investment move.

crypto-web3.title: Ex-White House Teleprompter Operator Fined for Prediction Market Insider Trading
crypto-web3.summary: The CFTC charged Gabriel Perez with insider trading after he leveraged advance access to presidential speeches to profit over $107,500 from prediction market contracts. The case highlights regulatory enforcement against market manipulation within emerging decentralized prediction platforms.

crypto-web3.title: Ninth Circuit deals blow to Kalshi in Nevada sports betting fight, challenging CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction claim
crypto-web3.summary: A federal appeals court ruled that Kalshi failed to demonstrate that federal law preempts Nevada's state betting authority, undermining the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction claim over prediction markets. The decision has significant implications for the regulatory framework governing crypto-based prediction platforms.

crypto-web3.title: Crypto market makers are cashing in on bitcoin's rally - without betting on direction
crypto-web3.summary: Sophisticated trading firms are generating yield from Bitcoin's rally above $80,000 through market-neutral strategies rather than directional bets. The activity highlights the growing sophistication of institutional participation in crypto markets through alternative profit mechanisms.

crypto-web3.title: Tokenized assets are busier than the data shows
crypto-web3.summary: Analysis suggests that the true utilization of tokenized assets may approach 20% when accounting for off-chain activity and correcting for data collection methodologies. The findings indicate that market participants may be underestimating blockchain-based asset adoption based on conventional metrics.

crypto-web3.title: Ditching 'digital gold': BPI study suggests everyday Americans prefer control and micro-investing
crypto-web3.summary: A new consumer survey indicates that mainstream Americans prioritize financial control and fractional investing over Bitcoin's traditional "digital gold" narrative. The findings suggest that current marketing approaches may not align with the preferences of broader adoption targets.

crypto-web3.title: Kalshi becomes exclusive prediction market partner of US Open: report
crypto-web3.summary: Kalshi secured an exclusive partnership agreement to operate prediction markets for the US Open, with competing platforms barred from advertising at the tournament. The deal represents a significant market expansion for the prediction market platform.

health-biotech.title: FDA approves Protagonist and Takeda's drug for rare blood cancer
health-biotech.summary: The FDA has approved Mimrylo, a novel therapeutic developed by Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics, for the treatment of polycythemia vera, a rare blood cancer. This approval represents a new treatment modality for patients with this hematologic malignancy.

health-biotech.title: Revolution drug heralded as a pancreatic cancer breakthrough cleared by FDA
health-biotech.summary: Rasonque has received FDA approval in an expedited manner, with the submission completed and cleared within one month, marking a significant paradigm shift for pancreatic cancer treatment. Analysts project this represents a highly lucrative drug launch for this notoriously difficult-to-treat malignancy.

health-biotech.title: Once-weekly oral antiretroviral therapy for HIV
health-biotech.summary: The ISLEND-2 trial demonstrates the efficacy of islatravir, a once-weekly oral antiretroviral therapy for HIV that represents a significant advance over traditional daily dosing regimens. This development marks a major shift in HIV treatment accessibility and patient adherence potential.

health-biotech.title: Arrowhead claims safety edge over Ionis as triglyceride battle draws closer
health-biotech.summary: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals' RNA interference drug Redemplo demonstrated superior safety and efficacy profiles compared to competitors in late-stage trials for patients with elevated triglycerides. The data positions Arrowhead competitively in the emerging triglyceride-lowering therapeutic market.

health-biotech.title: AstraZeneca's relaxin pill shows promise in mid-stage heart failure trial
health-biotech.summary: AstraZeneca's oral relaxin agonist demonstrated the ability to improve cardiac function in select patients in a Phase 2 heart failure trial, representing a partial success for this novel therapeutic mechanism. The results suggest potential clinical utility despite incomplete efficacy across the trial population.

health-biotech.title: Alnylam defends heart disease drugs after failure of AstraZeneca's Wainua
health-biotech.summary: Following AstraZeneca's trial failure with Wainua, Alnylam Pharmaceuticals has launched a defensive campaign for its own heart disease medications in the RNA interference space. The setback has intensified scrutiny on the viability of this drug class for cardiovascular indications.

health-biotech.title: Expanding regulatory T cells to treat atopic dermatitis
health-biotech.summary: Recent advances in atopic dermatitis treatment have evolved significantly over the past decade, with novel approaches targeting regulatory T cell expansion now emerging as treatment options. This represents a substantial shift from previous therapeutic paradigms in managing this burdensome inflammatory skin disease.

health-biotech.title: [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-sensitive prostate cancer
health-biotech.summary: Lutetium-177 PSMA-617, a radioligand therapy targeting prostate-specific membrane antigen, continues to expand its clinical application following initial 2022 approval based on the VISION trial. This therapy delivers targeted beta-particle radiation to PSMA-expressing tumor cells and the surrounding microenvironment.

health-biotech.title: Spyre tumbles as immune drug misses mark in rheumatoid arthritis
health-biotech.summary: Spyre Therapeutics experienced significant market capitalization erosion following disappointing clinical trial results for its TL1A-blocking immune therapy in rheumatoid arthritis. The data raised substantive questions regarding the clinical impact and market potential of this protein target in autoimmune disease.

health-biotech.title: Biohaven trades cash for 'upside' with $795M epilepsy drug deal
health-biotech.summary: Facing financial constraints following multiple research setbacks, Biohaven Pharmaceuticals divested its most advanced epilepsy candidate in an $795 million transaction to preserve capital. The deal was characterized by analysts as a surprising strategic shift for the company.

cybersecurity.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
cybersecurity.summary: A 26-year-old Canadian cybercriminal has pleaded guilty to orchestrating computer fraud and extortion attacks against over 165 organizations using Snowflake's cloud data storage platform. The defendant also admitted to stealing call and text history records from more than 100 million AT&T customers, marking one of the most consequential cybercrime cases of 2024.

cybersecurity.title: Two Alleged 'TeamPCP' Hackers Arrested in Australia
cybersecurity.summary: Australian Federal Police have arrested two suspects aged 21 and 23 in connection with TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime syndicate responsible for the longest running software supply chain attack campaign on record. The group is accused of creating malicious open-source software to extort thousands of organizations.

cybersecurity.title: Chinese Routers Sold Worldwide Contain Backdoors
cybersecurity.summary: ZBT routers distributed globally as white-label products have been discovered to contain multiple backdoors implanted by the manufacturer, potentially compromising network security for an untold number of organizations and individuals worldwide. The discovery highlights supply chain vulnerabilities in networking hardware.

cybersecurity.title: Chrome Web Store Extensions Caught Stealing Crypto, Browser Data
cybersecurity.summary: Multiple malicious extensions in the Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge web stores deployed a framework designed to steal cryptocurrency, sensitive data, and browser history while injecting ClickFix phishing lures. The discovery underscores the ongoing risk of compromised extensions in mainstream browser marketplaces.

cybersecurity.title: FulcrumSec Claims Manchester Airports Hack, Theft of 86 GB of Data
cybersecurity.summary: Threat actor FulcrumSec claims to have stolen 86 GB of data from Manchester Airports Group, with BleepingComputer validating samples containing detailed customer booking and travel information. The breach represents a significant compromise of traveler personal and sensitive data.

cybersecurity.title: Anthropic Warns Infostealer Malware Is Hijacking Claude Sessions to Drain Usage
cybersecurity.summary: Anthropic has alerted Claude users that infostealer malware infections are stealing active login sessions, allowing attackers to access accounts and consume API usage quotas without authorization. The advisory highlights the growing threat of credential theft targeting AI service platforms.

cybersecurity.title: TerminalFix Uses Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs to Deploy Reverse-Tunnel Backdoor
cybersecurity.summary: Microsoft has disclosed TerminalFix, a ClickFix variant that tricks users into executing malicious commands through Windows Terminal or PowerShell rather than the Run dialog, significantly increasing the likelihood of successful exploitation. The attack leverages fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA prompts to appear legitimate.

cybersecurity.title: Lessons Learned from CISA's Recent GitHub Leak
cybersecurity.summary: CISA released a postmortem analysis of a significant data leak in which a contractor exposed dozens of internal credentials, including AWS Govcloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months before discovery by KrebsOnSecurity. Security experts highlight the incident as a critical case study for credential management and incident response procedures.

cybersecurity.title: Two Unitree G1 EDU Humanoid Robot Flaws Enable Root RCE, One Starts Over Bluetooth
cybersecurity.summary: Security researcher Olivier Laflamme has disclosed two root remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-76639 and CVE-2026-76640) in Unitree G1 EDU humanoid robots, including a Bluetooth Low Energy attack path that can compromise the device's Locomotion PC. The vulnerabilities demonstrate emerging security risks in robotic systems.

cybersecurity.title: Who's Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out
cybersecurity.summary: A new free service called DecryptAds has been launched to help users identify which entities are responsible for targeted advertising and data harvesting across websites and mobile applications. The tool scrapes and correlates adtech data previously fragmented across advertising platforms, providing transparency into digital tracking practices.

startups-vc.title: Socure Secures $156M at $5.2B Valuation, Acquires AI Fraud Investigation Startup Fravity
startups-vc.summary: Identity verification and fraud prevention company Socure announced a $156 million strategic growth investment at a $5.2 billion valuation. The company is also acquiring agentic AI startup Fravity to integrate into its RiskOS platform as RiskOS_Agents, demonstrating the trend of well-funded startups acquiring specialized AI capabilities.

startups-vc.title: Viral AI startup Instinct has raised $350M at a $2.5B valuation
startups-vc.summary: One-year-old AI startup Instinct has achieved a $2.5 billion valuation after raising $350 million, demonstrating explosive growth and significant investor appetite for emerging AI companies. The company's rapid ascent has generated considerable hype alongside privacy concerns regarding its technology.

startups-vc.title: The Week's 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Defense Tech, AI Tools And Infrastructure Lead The Way
startups-vc.summary: The largest funding round of the week went to Castelion, a defense tech startup developing hypersonic missiles, with other significant capital flowing to companies in AI inference, video creation, data centers, and voice-to-text technologies. The funding landscape reflects intense competition in AI-related sectors and critical infrastructure development.

startups-vc.title: Startups Are Still Acquiring Startups, Led By Ultra-High-Valuation Unicorns
startups-vc.summary: Well-funded startups continue to acquire other companies at accelerating rates as a faster alternative to building technologies in-house, particularly amid competitive pressures in the AI sector. This consolidation trend reflects the premium placed on speed and technological capability acquisition in high-growth markets.

startups-vc.title: This former PG&E engineer is building a 'Google Maps for the underground'
startups-vc.summary: A startup founded by a former PG&E engineer has raised $26 million in Series A funding to develop underground infrastructure mapping technology that streamlines utility and construction work. The platform aims to reduce operational complexity and regulatory friction in the largely unmapped subsurface sector.

startups-vc.title: Fashion startup Atorie raises $9.5M to bring consumers luxury goods without the markup
startups-vc.summary: Fashion startup Atorie has secured $9.5 million in funding to disrupt the luxury goods market by selling directly to consumers handbags and clothing manufactured from identical materials and facilities as high-end brands. The model bypasses traditional retail markups by eliminating intermediaries in the luxury supply chain.

startups-vc.title: Owner.com Did an AI Rebuild to Accelerate Past $100M ARR. The 7 Top Lessons, and What It Takes to Copy Them
startups-vc.summary: Restaurant software company Owner.com achieved over $100 million in annual recurring revenue following a three-year AI-driven product rebuild from web and online ordering to AI-centric platform. The transformation demonstrates how established SaaS companies are leveraging AI to unlock new growth acceleration, overcoming initial customer skepticism about AI adoption.

startups-vc.title: Craft's Ilya Levtov Never Learned To Code. He Built A Software Company Anyway.
startups-vc.summary: Craft CEO Ilya Levtov, a Juilliard-trained cellist with no coding background, successfully launched supply chain intelligence software company and secured venture funding despite never writing a line of code. The case study highlights that diverse professional backgrounds can create successful technology founders when paired with strong domain expertise and strategic vision.

startups-vc.title: As electric two-wheelers gain a foothold, Belgian startup Any bets on cargo space
startups-vc.summary: Belgian startup Any has launched LUV1, a modular electric motorcycle featuring 120 liters of cargo capacity designed for commercial and personal use cases such as carrying equipment or pets. The product positions itself in the growing electric two-wheeler market by addressing practical storage limitations of existing vehicles.

startups-vc.title: Liux's Big microcar bets on sustainability to create differentiation in crowded EV market
startups-vc.summary: Spanish startup Liux is challenging established Chinese competitors in the microcar segment with an electric vehicle designed around sustainability principles. The company attempts to differentiate in an increasingly crowded market by emphasizing environmental responsibility alongside vehicle affordability and practicality.

energy-climate.title: Trump's energy policy could cost US 540 GW of renewables, says NRDC
energy-climate.summary: The Natural Resources Defense Council warns that Trump administration energy policies could eliminate over 540 gigawatts of anticipated renewable energy capacity, representing more than half of expected U.S. renewable energy additions. The analysis highlights the significant impact of policy reversals on the trajectory of the American energy transition.

energy-climate.title: Analysis: Weaker EV targets could cost UK consumers £3bn a year by 2030
energy-climate.summary: A UK government consultation proposing weaker electric vehicle targets could impose annual costs of £3 billion on consumers by 2030, according to analysis. The policy shift would delay the transition to lower-emission transportation and increase long-term consumer expenses.

energy-climate.title: Trump declares emergency, moves to block some foreign-made equipment from grid
energy-climate.summary: The Trump administration has declared an emergency and initiated restrictions on foreign-made equipment for the electrical grid, citing national security concerns. Equipment manufacturers have requested clarification on implementation rules, particularly for software and digital products where country of origin may be ambiguous.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: What is in China's new five-year plan for climate change?
energy-climate.summary: China has unveiled its 15th five-year plan dedicated to national climate change response, outlining strategies for emissions reduction and climate adaptation. The plan signals China's continued commitment to climate action amid global decarbonization efforts.

energy-climate.title: Data center load made up 9% of PJM wholesale costs so far in 2026: market monitor
energy-climate.summary: Data center electricity demand accounted for 9 percent of wholesale power costs in the PJM Interconnection during 2026, as overall wholesale costs surged 46 percent to $56.7 billion year-to-date. The dramatic increase reflects rising energy and capacity costs driven partly by growing data center consumption.

energy-climate.title: Factcheck: 10 flaws in the Conservative report on 'cheap power'
energy-climate.summary: Carbon Brief identifies ten significant flaws in a Conservative opposition report arguing that UK electricity prices are excessive and could be reduced through alternative policies. The analysis scrutinizes claims about energy costs and policy effectiveness in the UK power sector.

energy-climate.title: Explainer: How the 'super El Niño' will reshape the world's weather
energy-climate.summary: The world is currently experiencing what is expected to become the strongest El Niño on record, known as a 'super El Niño,' which will significantly alter global weather patterns. The phenomenon has substantial implications for climate and weather-related impacts across multiple regions.

energy-climate.title: Ohio ratepayer advocate urges FERC to resolve 3-year-old local transmission complaint
energy-climate.summary: The Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel has urged federal regulators to address a three-year-old transmission complaint, noting that utilities have approved over $4.3 billion in local transmission projects without adequate regulatory oversight. The complaint highlights concerns about transmission planning governance and consumer protection.

energy-climate.title: Calix selects Perdaman as hydrogen partner for Zesty Green Iron project
energy-climate.summary: Calix and Perdaman have entered into an agreement to develop a hydrogen supply solution for Calix's Zesty Green Iron Demonstration Project. The partnership aims to advance clean hydrogen production for industrial decarbonization applications.

energy-climate.title: Europe's solar resource surplus continues before late-August cloud shift
energy-climate.summary: European solar irradiance averaged 5 percent above the 2007-2025 norm in August 2026, with approximately three-quarters of the continent receiving above-average solar resources driven by persistent high pressure systems. Weather patterns shifted later in the month as cooler, cloudier conditions reduced gains in western Europe.

asia-pacific.title: Small state, big agenda: Singapore prepares to steer Asean through crisis
asia-pacific.summary: Singapore will assume the ASEAN chairmanship on January 1, taking leadership of the 60-year-old bloc during a period of global fracturing and geopolitical instability. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong emphasized the city-state's commitment to navigating regional challenges and enhancing ASEAN's collective response to international crises.

asia-pacific.title: Citi's China-US corridor thrives as mainland firms hedge risks amid trade turbulence
asia-pacific.summary: Despite escalating US-China trade friction, Chinese firms are intensifying corporate activity with the United States through aggressive risk-hedging strategies to maintain global market share. Citi reports steady revenue growth on its North America-China corridor as mainland companies deploy financial instruments and leverage global institutions to navigate complex supply chains and trade barriers.

asia-pacific.title: Huawei and Apple bend to a tougher market with foldable phones as memory crunch bites
asia-pacific.summary: Apple and Huawei's anticipated foldable phone launches next week aim to revitalize a subdued global smartphone market facing an estimated 17 percent decline in 2026. Apple's September 9 keynote, featuring its first foldable iPhone and new CEO John Ternus, represents a critical moment as both tech giants navigate supply chain constraints and market saturation.

asia-pacific.title: India is producing millions of graduates, but where are the jobs?
asia-pacific.summary: Youth-led protests across India over exam irregularities have exposed deeper anxiety surrounding widespread graduate unemployment in the country. The employment crisis reflects structural challenges in India's labor market despite record numbers of university graduates entering the workforce.

asia-pacific.title: Golden hour: why Hong Kong may finally succeed in becoming precious metal's trading hub
asia-pacific.summary: Hong Kong is positioning itself as a global gold trading hub comparable to New York and London, leveraging its duty-free status and proximity to major gold-consuming markets in Asia. Previous skepticism about this ambition is fading as regulatory and market conditions increasingly favor the city's emergence as a premier international precious metals exchange.

asia-pacific.title: 'Zero sense' to view Hong Kong, Singapore as enemies in changing world: envoy
asia-pacific.summary: Singapore's consul general in Hong Kong advocates for expanded cooperation between the two financial centers, arguing that Asia's regional growth is sufficient to accommodate both as complementary hubs rather than competitors. The envoy emphasized the importance of collaborative efforts to capitalize on capital inflows into the Asia-Pacific region.

asia-pacific.title: South Korea's SK On signs energy storage battery deal with US firm NeoVolta Power
asia-pacific.summary: SK On, South Korea's leading battery manufacturer, has concluded a strategic partnership with US-based NeoVolta Power to expand energy storage solutions. The deal reflects growing collaboration in the critical energy storage sector amid global transitions toward renewable energy and grid stabilization technologies.

asia-pacific.title: At your service: Hong Kong welcomes first humanoid robot-run convenience stores
asia-pacific.summary: Hong Kong is opening its first humanoid robot-operated convenience stores through a Beijing-based embodied-intelligence robotics company, marking the firm's first international expansion outside mainland China. The company plans to establish approximately 10 additional outlets across the city as it tests its autonomous retail model in global markets.

asia-pacific.title: China teen with zero programming skills earns US$2,600 in 3 days selling AI study app
asia-pacific.summary: A 13-year-old Shanghai student with no programming background developed an artificial intelligence application to assist parents in monitoring children's study habits, earning 18,000 yuan (US$2,600) at a national AI product competition in Hangzhou. The case exemplifies China's democratization of AI tools and growing entrepreneurial opportunities for young people in the technology sector.

asia-pacific.title: Hong Kong WhatsApp hijacking scams surge 170% to nearly 2,000 cases
asia-pacific.summary: WhatsApp account hijacking scams in Hong Kong increased by nearly 170 percent to almost 2,000 cases during the first seven months of 2026, with reported losses totaling HK$146.3 million and individual victims losing up to HK$12.2 million. The surge represents a significant cybersecurity challenge for the city as fraudsters exploit messaging platform vulnerabilities to commit large-scale financial crimes.
